name: Dubhe
description: A naked-eye star 37.7 parsecs away, 17.0 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 95689: radius 17.03 +/- 0.13 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 6.419 +/- 0.041 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 95689: mass 3.44 +/- 0.11 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 95689: effective temperature 5012 +/- 65 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331, XHIP, HIP 54061: RV -9.4 +/- 0.3 km/s (quality D)

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 95689: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 26.54 +/- 0.48 mas, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A naked-eye star 38 parsecs away whose disc the NPOI measured: 17.0 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 6.419 milliarcseconds, which gives 17.03 solar radii and 5,012 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 95689: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff
